neighbours.label: 'if' (si, wenn) opening a parenthetical hedge after a comma (difficult, if not impossible / few, if any), vs conditional 'if' introducing a condition
fire: The repair will be costly, if not impossible, without the original parts.
There were few, if any, survivors from the shipwreck.
His speech was clever, if a little long.
The new policy has done little, if anything, to cut prices.
The road is passable, if not exactly comfortable, in winter.
Most, if not all, of the tickets have been sold.
The hotel was pleasant, if somewhat overpriced.
Very few people, if any, still remember the old mill.
quiet: The repair will be costly if the original parts are missing.
There were few survivors from the shipwreck.
His speech will be clever if he prepares it carefully.
The new policy has done little to cut prices.
The road is passable in winter if you have chains.
Most of the tickets will be sold if the weather is good.
The hotel was pleasant and somewhat overpriced.
Ask the old miller if you want to know the history.

predictions: Comma-hedge 'if' reaches 0.4-0.9; conditional 'if' and hedges built with 'or even' stay under 0.15.
notes: Card: top 32 peak on ' if' x17 after a comma in 'if not', 'if any', plus ' si', ' wenn'.
